note: Curated highlight-eval fixtures. Segments are the transcript source of truth; the harness expands each into contract-valid words. Expected ranges are human picks. Cases are designed to discriminate: some align hook keywords with the true highlight (heuristic-friendly), others carry the key insight without any hook word (LLM-friendly). Real transcripts can be dropped in later using the same schema.

cases.note: Hook keywords sit in the true highlight — heuristic-friendly.

segments.text: Welcome back to the channel. Today we are editing a short clip.
First, open your project and find the sequence you want to share.
Then choose the in and out points on the timeline.
The most common mistake is exporting before you check the audio levels.
Always listen through with headphones at least once.
Next, open the export dialog and pick the social preset.
The best preset for shorts is 1080 by 1920 at a reasonable bitrate.
If the file is too big, lower the bitrate before anything else.
That is it. Go export your clip and post it.

cases.note: Key insight has no hook word; 'how'/'key' segments are distractors — LLM-friendly.

segments.text: So I was talking to a founder last week about their launch.
They had this beautiful product and zero attention on it.
How do you even start building an audience from nothing?
I told him something he did not want to hear that day.
Revenue follows attention, not the other way around.
So he started posting his build in public every morning.
The key is showing up every single day for a whole year.

cases.note: Two true highlights; one carries no hook word — tests multi-highlight recall.

segments.text: Today we are making the simplest pasta of your life.
Boil more water than you think you need. That is the first rule.
Salt the water until it tastes like a mild broth, not the sea.
Save a cup of the pasta water before you drain anything.
Why does that starchy water matter so much?
It emulsifies the sauce and makes it cling to every strand.
The best time to add the sauce is right off the heat.
Finish with olive oil, pepper, and a ridiculous amount of cheese.

cases.note: Expected range spans two segments — tests boundary-tolerant matching.

segments.text: Alright, let us break down that last team fight.
He peaked the same angle three times. Never do that.
The important thing here is the timing on the ultimate.
He used it one second too early and the whole play died.
How do you practice that timing? Go into the training range.
Spend ten minutes a day on cooldown tracking and it compounds.
The best players are not the fastest, they are the most patient.
That is the review. Go fix your peaks.

cases.note: Retention insight without hook words; 'how'/'key' distractors — LLM-friendly.

segments.text: In 1885 a German psychologist wrote about the forgetting curve.
He found that memory drops off steeply within the first hour.
How do students usually fight this? They reread their notes.
Rereading feels productive but it barely moves the retention line.
Testing yourself on the material is what actually rebuilds the trace.
The key is spacing those tests out over days, not hours.
So close the book and write everything you remember from it.

cases.note: Pivotal moment phrased plainly; hook words live in the wrong segments.

segments.text: What was the moment you knew it would work?
Honestly it was a complaint email from a customer in Ohio.
She said the app saved her two hours every single morning.
We had three hundred users at the time and I felt like a failure.
That email is still pinned above my desk three years later.
Why? Because it told me the problem was real and painful.
Everything after that was just execution and patience.
